selection_reason: LightGBM selected because it has the best validation MAE (6789.74), and among the competitive models it has the smallest artifact (2.40 MB) followed by lowest single-row latency (9.77 ms).
data_quality_notes: Prices are US dollars and mileage is in miles (verified from '$' and 'mi.' formatting).

The 'clean_title' column only contains 'Yes' for 3413 rows and is missing for 596 rows; it has no usable variance and missingness is correlated with listing source, so it is excluded from model features.
The fuel_type column uses '–' and 'not supported' as placeholders; these are treated as unknown and inferred as Electric when the engine description is electric.
Brand values 'Land', 'Aston' and 'Alfa' are truncated forms of Land Rover, Aston Martin and Alfa Romeo; they are repaired using the first token of the model column.
The engine column is free text (1146 unique strings). It is parsed into horsepower, displacement, cylinder count, forced-induction and electric indicators.

One Maserati Quattroporte (2005) is listed at $2,954,083, which is implausible for the model and is retained as an anomaly rather than silently deleted. MAE training limits its impact; metrics with and without outliers are discussed in the evaluation report.
No exact duplicate rows exist. Three vehicle keys appear twice (6 rows), likely duplicate listings; a grouped split keeps them in the same partition to prevent leakage.
